residue.text: Retained stage1 replay detail, also supplied in both concerns: inspect/select K2 at 0-1, commit 1-2; inspect/select K5 at 2-3, commit 3-4; inspect/select K7 at 4-5, commit 5-6; refresh 6-7. Log times, snapshots, retained rows, intended keys, actual writes and final statuses. This replay remains proposed.

Retained diagnostic proposal: cross changing/frozen snapshots with row/key binding under identical select-refresh-commit actions. Hypothesis: changing-plus-row writes K5; other arms write K2. These prospective controls test selection identity; a diagnostic incorrect-key write fails the unchanged valued outcome.

Retained unresolved return-link proposal, sharpened by INV: enable/suppress mismatch-triggered requests with equal-duration replacement inspections. Hypothesis: recurrence attributable to return refresh disappears when that link is suppressed. INV additionally proposes injecting/withholding mismatch notifications at matched gates to separate mismatch -> refresh from refresh -> mismatch. An extra request alone proves neither changed selection nor recurrence; retain final freshness and timing constraints.

Retained boundary material from stage1 and concerns: equal S2 scores cannot identify K5 versus K7; verify immutable keys. Scope remains eight invented records. Real binding, detection and interruption costs are unknown; concurrency, deletion and load failures are excluded. Production and human-usability resources are absent.

summary.text: Stipulated evidence: selecting K2, then refreshing to S1, then committing through retained row 2 writes K5. Stage1 and both concerns agree this establishes one synthetic miswrite through the specified identity interface. Repeated feedback and completed reliable correction remain unobserved.

Rival Hypothesis A, retained from stage1 and tested by ATT/INV: refresh immediately before every commit is necessary for reliable correction. It predicts failure on the proposed seven-minute replay without intermediate refresh. The procedure asserts necessity; C5 mandates only final freshness. Keep this branch unresolved pending replay evidence.

Rival Hypothesis B, retained from stage1 and developed by ATT/INV: keep S0 loaded through fixed-key commits, then refresh once. Predicted writes are K2, K5 and K7 only; key-persistent statuses survive final S2 loading at minute seven. Verified success would falsify A within this model. No such success is supplied.

Both branches face identical acceptance criteria: exactly K2/K5/K7 checked, five others unchecked, no incorrect-key write even if repaired, read-only scores, latest snapshot before submission and at most ten sequential simulated minutes. Compare complete write logs and final state; defer branch selection until observations arrive.
